ideal: Bc8 drops the a8-rook for a pawn: 17.Qf3 threatens mate on f7, forcing 17...O-O, and 18.Qxa8 wins the rook.
note: Qf3 mates on f7, forcing Black to castle before White takes on a8.

ideal: h3 misses Nxe5, winning a bishop and a pawn for the knight after 12...Be6 13.Bxe6 fxe5.
note: The f7 mate is parried by Be6; bishops and pawns are the real prize.

ideal: Qf3 drops the queen and the h-pawn: 18...Qxf3 19.Kg1 Qxh3, with mate on g4 to follow.
note: Queen and pawn fall at once, and Rg4 mate then forces Be6, dropping the bishop too.

ideal: h5 misses Bxc3+, winning two pawns: 21.Kf1 Rd8 22.f3 exf3 23.gxf3 Bxf3.
note: Two pawns fall while the king sits safe on f1; castling is a footnote.

ideal: Rxe7+ drops the rook for the knight after 30.Rxe7.
note: Rook for knight is the damage; Re8 mate never lands because Kf8 parries.

ideal: Nc6 drops a pawn to 11.Nxf6+ Kd8.
note: One check takes the f6-pawn and drives the king out of castling.

ideal: Bb6 drops a rook, a knight and two pawns for a bishop: 18...Qxc3+ 19.Kd1 Qxa1+ 20.Ke2 Qxa2 21.Kf3 Qxc2.
note: The king runs while the queen takes rook, knight and two pawns; only a bishop comes back.

ideal: Ne2 drops a bishop and a pawn for the knight: 12...Nd3+ 13.Kd2 Qxf2 14.Kxd3 Qf5+ 15.Kd2 Ne4+ 16.Ke1 Nxg5.
note: Checks walk the king while Black nets bishop and pawn for knight; castling is incidental.

ideal: Nh4 misses Ng5, winning a bishop and a pawn for the knight: 10...h5 11.Nxe6 Bxe6 12.Rxe6+.
note: k0 invents Qd3/Qg6+/Kd8, and the real line ends with Black castling queenside.

ideal: Bb6 drops the queen and a pawn for the rook: 10.Bxf7+ Kf8 11.Re1 Qxe1+ 12.Kxe1.
note: Bxf7+ takes a pawn, drives the king out, and Re1 traps the queen.

ideal: Qxd8+ misses Bxf7+, winning a bishop and a knight: 7...Ke7 8.exf6+ gxf6 9.Qxg4.
note: Two pieces beat a queen trade; the e6 mate only forces Bh6.

ideal: h4 drops the queen: 13...Nd3+ 14.Kf1 Nxf4.
note: Nd3+ forces Kf1, hanging the queen; the lost castling is a footnote.

ideal: h6 misses Bxf2+, winning a pawn with check: 8.Kf1 leaves White unable to castle.
note: Bxf2+ takes the pawn with check; Kf1 keeps the bishop but loses castling.

ideal: Bg4 drops a pawn: 7.Bxf7+ Kxf7 8.Ng5+ Ke8 9.Qxg4.
note: Black loses all castling but lands safe on e8; the pawn is the damage.

ideal: Qxe4 misses Qh5+: 8.Bc4 threatens mate on f7, and 8...d5 drops the queen and a pawn for the bishop.
note: Bc4 mates on f7, forcing the d5 block that drops queen and pawn.

ideal: Nxg3 drops a knight and a pawn for the bishop: 22.fxg3 Be6 23.Qxb7.
note: Rxf8 mate is met by Be6; the damage is knight and pawn for bishop.

ideal: Qb5 misses Bd4, threatening mate on f1: 20.Ba3 must parry, and 20...Bxa1 wins a rook for the bishop.
note: Bd4 mates on f1, so Ba3 must parry and abandons a1.

ideal: Rf3 misses Qh6, threatening mate on g7: 26...Rxd3+ 27.Kc2 Rd2+ only checks, and 28.Qxd2 wins the rook for a pawn.
note: Only checks stall Qg7 mate, and they drop the rook.

ideal: Rfd8 loses the queen, a rook and the new queen for a knight and a pawn: 26.Rxe2 R2d7 27.Nxd8 Rxd8 28.f8=Q.
note: The b7 mate never lands because Bc6 parries; queen and rooks are the damage.

ideal: Ke8 allows 33.Rh7 with mate on h8: 33...Nxh3+ 34.Kh2 Rxg2+ only checks, and 35.Kxg2 wins the rook for two pawns.
note: Only checks stall Rh8 mate, and they sac the rook for two pawns.

ideal: Ne4 allows 20...Nf3+ 21.Kh1 Nxe1 with mate on g2: 22.Nxg5 must take the queen, and 22...Nxd3 wins a bishop.
note: Nxe1 mates on g2, forcing Nxg5, and Nxd3 then takes the bishop.

ideal: Qa4+ drops the bishop: 17...Bd7 18.Qc2 Rxh5.
note: Rxh5 takes the bishop and mates on h2; h3 is forced but secondary.

ideal: Be3 drops a bishop: 17.Qxe3 Nb4 18.Bxd7+ Kxd7.
note: Bxd7+ forces the king recapture, costing castling on top of the bishop.

ideal: R4e7 misses Rxe3, when mate on h3 forces 24.fxe3, and 24...Qf2+ 25.Kh1 Qxc2 wins two bishops for the rook.
note: Mate on h3 forces fxe3 and the Kh1 walk that drops the second bishop.

ideal: bxc5 misses dxc6, winning a knight for a pawn: 13...axb4 14.cxd7+.
note: Knight for pawn is the prize; the king walk to d7 is extra.

ideal: gxh5 allows 22.Qg3 with mate on g7: 22...Nd3+ 23.Bxd3 Qxe3+ only sacs, and 24.Qxe3 wins the queen for a pawn.
note: Qg3 mates on g7, forcing the Nd3/Qxe3 sac that drops the queen.

ideal: Kd6 drops the queen and a bishop: 18.Nxc4+ Kd7 19.Nxa3.
note: Queen and bishop fall for free; Bxf5 mate only forces g6.

ideal: Qe8+ hangs the queen to 28...Qxe8+.
note: The queen is hung outright; the e2 mate wins a bishop on top.

ideal: Nb5 misses dxe6, winning the queen and a bishop for the knight: 9...Bxf3 10.exf7+ Kxf7 11.Bxf3.
note: dxe6 takes the queen first; the lost castling is a footnote.

ideal: exd5 drops a rook and a bishop for a pawn: 27.Rxe8+ Bf8 28.Bxf8.
note: Rook and bishop for a pawn; Bh6 mate only forces h5.
